messages:
PagerDuty: INCIDENT ALERT - High rate of 401s from service-account tokens observed on auth-proxy. Priority: P1. link: https://pagerduty.example/incidents/INC-9234
AlertBot: Autodetected anomaly: credential-fuzzing-pattern flagged — 120 unique IPs in 3m, 9 distinct user agents. Potential brute force or scanning.
jordan (oncall): I’m on it. pulling logs now. which env?
AlertBot: Affected environment: production-us-east-1. Top targets: /v1/auth/session, /v1/token/validate
ria (security): tagging as sec-incident. Jordan, if these are service account tokens we should rotate any exposed keys immediately and disable token issuance for a short window.
jordan (oncall): ok will gather example hits, then take the edge rule to block the offending IPs for now. Samir, can you stand by for rotation?
samir (infra): standing by. if we need key rotation I have the script: 
```
./infra/tools/rotate-service-account.sh --project redwood-prod --sa inference-proxy --rotate-keys
```
katie (sre): also recommend enabling temporary rate-limit on token endpoint: `X-RateLimit-Policy: strict` until we validate.
jordan (oncall): grabbing examples... filtering by status=401 and path contains token/validate. one sample: `ip=52.14.233.87 ua=Go-http-client/2 token_id=svc-xy123`
ria (security): that token_id looks like an internal service token. Need to determine if token was exfiltrated or guessed. Samir, can you check recent token minting logs for svc-xy123?
samir (infra): query in progress against audit-db: `SELECT * FROM token_issuance WHERE token_id='svc-xy123' ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 50;`
DevSec Bot: Runbook matched: "credential-fuzzing-detection". Recommended actions: 1) block IP ranges, 2) rotate service tokens with 3-min grace, 3) enable fallback policies. https://runbooks.internal/CredentialFuzzing
jordan (oncall): executing edge block for top 25 IPs now via waf console. patch: `waf.block_ips(ids.txt)`
AlertBot: WAF blocks applied. Traffic for those IPs dropped by 92% in next 60s.
katie (sre): confirming, latency unchanged. good. Jordan, how many tokens look suspicious total?
jordan (oncall): initial scan shows 7 service tokens with suspicious validate events in the last 30m: svc-xy123, svc-ab987, svc-lm402, svc-zz001, svc-qa555, svc-batch3, svc-cache2
ria (security): prepare to rotate those seven. Samir, coordinate with me on staggered rotation so we don’t break long-running jobs. Use canary rotation: rotate one SA key at a time and monitor.
samir (infra): acknowledged. plan: rotate in this order: svc-xy123 -> svc-ab987 -> svc-lm402 -> svc-zz001 -> svc-qa555 -> svc-batch3 -> svc-cache2. each rotate: generate new key, update secrets in vault, deploy a 5-min canary to test clients, then revoke old key after 10m. Script: 
```
# rotate single token
./infra/tools/rotate-service-account.sh --sa <sa> --generate-new-key --update-vault --deploy-canary --revoke-old --notify slack:incidents
```
jordan (oncall): executing rotate for svc-xy123 now. I’ll watch auth logs.
DevSec Bot: Notifying dependent teams: #devex, #integrations, #customer-success. Template: "We are rotating service credentials for a subset of tokens due to suspicious activity. Short risk of temporary failures — contact oncall for issues"
ria (security): we should also notify any customers potentially impacted if tokens map to customer-facing integrations. Jordan, any mapping?
jordan (oncall): quick lookup: svc-xy123 -> internal proxy, no direct customer mapping. svc-qa555 might be tied to partner ingestion. I’ll flag that to CS after initial rotation.
samir (infra): svc-xy123 rotated: new key deployed to vault, canary deployed to two nodes. Monitoring auth success.
AlertBot: canary auth success rate: 100% over 3m. No errors.
jordan (oncall): revoking old key for svc-xy123 now.
AlertBot: old key revoked. No immediate spike in errors.
katie (sre): run a quick grep for retries/errors across backend logs targeting token failures: `rg "svc-xy123|401" /var/logs/services/* -n`
ria (security): logging full set of suspicious IPs and metadata to the incident ticket. running deep forensics on user agents and ASN.
jordan (oncall): moving to svc-ab987 rotation next. Samir, go ahead when ready.
samir (infra): starting rotation for svc-ab987.
DevSec Bot: Reminder: update the incident timeline and set incident stage to "mitigated" when >4 tokens rotated and WAF blocks holding.
jordan (oncall): after 3 tokens rotated and WAF blocks in place, traffic pattern returned to baseline. draft mitigation status: WAF blocks + token rotations ongoing.
ria (security): set short-lived policy: disable new token issuance for affected SA roles for 15m to limit window. Jordan / Samir coordinate with deployments that need fresh tokens.
samir (infra): issuance disabled for `service-accounts:ingest` role.
AlertBot: external scanning activity subsided. 401 spike down to background rate.
katie (sre): monitoring dashboards look green. but keep alert thresholds active.
jordan (oncall): rotating last few tokens now, will handoff to Ria for post-incident review. Estimated finish in ~18m.
ria (security): once rotations complete, I’ll run token integrity checks and open a customer-impact assessment if we find any customer-linked tokens. Also prepare an email draft for CS if needed.
DevSec Bot: Incident notes saved to ticket INC-9234. Actions taken: WAF blocks, rotated 7 service tokens, disabled issuance for affected role, canaries successful, old keys revoked.
jordan (oncall): final confirm — all 7 rotated, old keys revoked, WAF blocks still in place. No customer-facing outages reported. handing off to ria for RCA and follow-up. :white_check_mark:
ria (security): taking over. I’ll schedule a 1-hour postmortem in #incidents-postmortems for 17:00 UTC and include action items: tighter token issuance alerts, add automated dev keys inventory, expand runbook for staggered rotation.
katie (sre): thumbs up. also recommend increasing retention on token issuance logs to 90 days for forensics.
jordan (oncall): thanks team, paging cleared.
PagerDuty: INCIDENT INC-9234 status: Resolved -> Monitoring. Affected services: auth-proxy. Severity downgraded.
DevSec Bot: Closing checklist: add incident labels: security, auth, token-rotation, runbook-update.
ria (security): closing notes: probable credential fuzzing via mass token validate attempts. No evidence of exfil from storage. Follow-ups: rotate any tokens not covered by automated inventory, add anomaly detector tuned for service-token validate patterns.
